Over 8,055 ES windows (p<=30000, 5 windows each) DP and enumeration agreed everywhere and the bound held (max ratio 1.000, with equality at omega=1); sum of DP ops 1.03M vs sum tau 0.78M, so neither dominates at these sizes. The premise that omega is the tractable parameter is not supported; the modulus r is.

summary: Benchmarked the residue-reachability DP for N=M^2 (p<=3000, m in [50,999], 300 cases) with a Python set, a Python-int bitset (per-bit gather) and numpy gather; all three gave identical sets. summary: Macbeath-type check (scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_Z0154.py): for each ES triple (x,y,z) of 4/n, n=5..40, and q∈{5,7,11,13}, searched for a generating pair A,B∈PSL(2,q) with ord(A)|x, ord(B)|y, ord(AB)|z (generation checked by BFS). summary: PROVED: pairwise-coprime ES denominators are impossible. If gcd(x,yz)=1 then from 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) we get x | n·yz, so x | n; likewise y|n, z|n, so xyz | n, n = m·xyz, and 4 = m(xy+yz+zx) with xy+yz+zx ≥ 3 and no integer solution (only (1,1,1) gives 4/3). So no Brieskorn link Σ(x,y,z) of an ES triple is a Z-homology sphere (Brieskorn: H1=0 iff pairwise coprime). Numerically: 85,311 unordered ES solutions for n≤400, 0 pairwise coprime (scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_Z0157.py).
not_done: H1 orders (torsion of H1) of the non-sphere links were not computed; the Brieskorn criterion was used as a standard fact, not checked against a source.
next: Compute |H1| of Σ(x,y,z) for a few solutions via the Milnor-fibre monodromy (Δ(1)) and compare with the gcd skeleton.

summary: Premise check: the item's relaxation is wrong. {1/x+1/y+1/z = 4/p} is a non-convex surface; its convex relaxation {x,y,z>0 : 1/x+1/y+1/z ≤ 4/p} is convex (sum of convex functions) but contains many lattice points that are not solutions (e.g. (N,N,N) for N ≥ 3p/4), so it is not lattice-free and Khinchine flatness yields no bound on the lattice width. The step as stated (width of the slice body for hard primes) therefore returns nothing usable.
